title: WHAT IS PHP?
intro: PHP is a server-side programming language. The web server runs your PHP code and sends only the result (usually HTML) to the browser. Visitors never see your PHP source.
body:
## How a PHP page works - The browser asks the server for `page.php`. - The server runs the PHP code inside the file. - Whatever the code outputs (with `echo`) is sent back to the browser as HTML. ## Your first script PHP code goes between ``. Every statement ends with a semicolon. ```php ` is a short way to write ``. ```php

Welcome

Today is .

Good morning!

``` ## Output and comments ```php TIP: Use `var_dump()` while debugging: it shows both the type and the value, so you can tell `"5"` (string) from `5` (int). > MISTAKE: A file that contains only PHP should leave out the closing `?>`. Any blank line after it would be sent to the browser by accident.
remember: PHP runs on the server; the browser only receives the output.
Code goes inside `<?php ... ?>` and statements end with `;`.
`echo` / `print` output text; `var_dump()` is for debugging.

title: VARIABLES & DATA TYPES
intro: A variable stores a value so you can use it later. In PHP every variable name starts with `$`, and you do not declare a type: PHP works it out from the value.
body:
## Creating variables

```php
<?php
$name = "Ana";      // string
$age = 20;          // int
$height = 1.65;     // float
$isStudent = true;  // bool
$nothing = null;    // null

echo "$name is $age years old.";
```
```output
Ana is 20 years old.
```

- Names start with a letter or underscore after the `$`: `$user_name` is valid, `$2user` is not.
- Names are case-sensitive: `$Age` and `$age` are different variables.

## The data types

```php
<?php
var_dump("hi", 7, 3.5, false, null, [1, 2]);
```
```output
string(2) "hi"
int(7)
float(3.5)
bool(false)
NULL
array(2) {
  [0]=>
  int(1)
  [1]=>
  int(2)
}
```

Check a type with `gettype()` or with the `is_*` functions: `is_int()`, `is_string()`, `is_array()`, `is_null()` and so on.

## Type juggling and casting

PHP converts types automatically when it needs to. You can also convert explicitly with a cast.

```php
<?php
echo "10" + 5, "\n";        // 15: the string becomes a number
echo (int) "42abc", "\n";   // 42
echo (string) 3.0, "\n";    // 3
var_dump((bool) "0");       // false
```
```output
15
42
3
bool(false)
```

These values are treated as **false**: `false`, `0`, `0.0`, `""`, `"0"`, `[]` and `null`. Everything else is true.

## isset() and empty()

```php
<?php
$a = 0;
$b = null;
var_dump(isset($a), isset($b), empty($a));
```
```output
bool(true)
bool(false)
bool(true)
```

## Constants

A constant holds a value that never changes. It has no `$` and is usually written in capitals.

```php
<?php
define("SITE_NAME", "CodeMaster");
const MAX_HP = 100;
echo SITE_NAME, " ", MAX_HP;
```
```output
CodeMaster 100
```

> MISTAKE: Using a variable that was never set gives an "Undefined variable" warning. Check it with `isset()` or give a default with `??`.
remember: Variables start with `$`; constants do not.
Types: string, int, float, bool, array, object, null.
`"0"`, `""`, `0`, `[]` and `null` are all false.

title: OPERATORS
intro: Operators do work on values: arithmetic, comparing, combining conditions and joining strings.
body:
## Arithmetic

```php
<?php
echo 7 + 2, " ", 7 - 2, " ", 7 * 2, " ", 7 / 2, " ", 7 % 2, " ", 2 ** 3;
```
```output
9 5 14 3.5 1 8
```

`%` is the remainder (modulo) and `**` is the power. `intdiv(7, 2)` gives the whole-number result 3.

## Assignment shortcuts

```php
<?php
$hp = 50;
$hp += 10;   // 60
$hp -= 5;    // 55
$hp *= 2;    // 110
$name = "Code";
$name .= "Master";
echo $hp, " ", $name;
```
```output
110 CodeMaster
```

## Increment and decrement

```php
<?php
$i = 5;
echo $i++, " ";  // prints 5, then $i becomes 6
echo ++$i;       // $i becomes 7, then prints 7
```
```output
5 7
```

## Comparison: == vs ===

`==` compares values after converting types. `===` also requires the same type. Prefer `===`.

```php
<?php
var_dump(5 == "5", 5 === "5", 5 != 6, 5 <=> 9);
```
```output
bool(true)
bool(false)
bool(true)
int(-1)
```

The spaceship operator `<=>` returns -1, 0 or 1. It is handy for sorting.

## Logical operators

```php
<?php
$hasKey = true;
$isBoss = false;
var_dump($hasKey && !$isBoss, $hasKey || $isBoss);
```
```output
bool(true)
bool(true)
```

## Ternary and null coalescing

```php
<?php
$score = 75;
echo $score >= 50 ? "Pass" : "Fail", "\n";
$data = [];
echo $data["name"] ?? "Guest";   // default when the key is missing or null
```
```output
Pass
Guest
```

> MISTAKE: `=` assigns, `==` compares. Writing `if ($x = 5)` sets $x to 5 and is always true.
remember: `%` = remainder, `**` = power, `.` = join strings.
Use `===` unless you really want type conversion.
`??` gives a default for missing or null values.

title: STRINGS
intro: Strings are text. PHP has many built-in functions for working with them.
body:
## Single vs double quotes

```php
<?php
$hero = "Knight";
echo "Hello $hero\n";      // variables and \n are expanded
echo 'Hello $hero\n';      // printed exactly as written
echo "\n";
echo "Level {$hero}s";     // braces mark where the variable ends
```
```output
Hello Knight
Hello $hero\n
Level Knights
```

## Joining strings

```php
<?php
$first = "Code";
$last = "Master";
echo $first . " " . $last;
```
```output
Code Master
```

## Common string functions

```php
<?php
$s = "Hello World";
echo strlen($s), "\n";               // 11
echo strtoupper($s), "\n";
echo strtolower($s), "\n";
echo ucfirst("php"), "\n";            // Php
echo substr($s, 0, 5), "\n";         // Hello
echo strpos($s, "World"), "\n";      // 6
echo str_replace("World", "PHP", $s), "\n";
echo trim("  spaced  "), "|";
```
```output
11
HELLO WORLD
hello world
Php
Hello
6
Hello PHP
spaced|
```

## Splitting and joining

```php
<?php
$parts = explode(",", "red,green,blue");
echo count($parts), "\n";
echo implode(" | ", $parts);
```
```output
3
red | green | blue
```

## Formatting

```php
<?php
printf("%s has %d HP (%.1f%%)\n", "Mage", 45, 45 / 60 * 100);
echo number_format(1234567.891, 2), "\n";
echo str_pad("7", 3, "0", STR_PAD_LEFT);
```
```output
Mage has 45 HP (75.0%)
1,234,567.89
007
```

## PHP 8 helpers

```php
<?php
var_dump(str_contains("dungeon", "geo"));
var_dump(str_starts_with("dungeon", "dun"));
var_dump(str_ends_with("dungeon", "on"));
```
```output
bool(true)
bool(true)
bool(true)
```

> MISTAKE: `strpos()` returns `0` when the text is at the start, and 0 is falsy. Always compare with `!== false`, or use `str_contains()`.
remember: Double quotes expand variables; single quotes do not.
String positions start at 0.
`explode()` splits a string into an array; `implode()` joins an array into a string.

title: ARRAYS
intro: An array holds many values in one variable. PHP arrays can use numbers (indexed) or names (associative) as keys.
body:
## Indexed arrays

```php
<?php
$items = ["Sword", "Shield", "Potion"];
echo $items[0], "\n";      // first item
$items[] = "Map";          // add to the end
echo count($items);
```
```output
Sword
4
```

## Associative arrays

```php
<?php
$hero = ["name" => "Ana", "hp" => 100, "class" => "Mage"];
echo $hero["name"], "\n";
$hero["hp"] -= 20;
foreach ($hero as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key: $value\n";
}
```
```output
Ana
name: Ana
hp: 80
class: Mage
```

## Multidimensional arrays

```php
<?php
$party = [
    ["name" => "Ana", "hp" => 80],
    ["name" => "Ben", "hp" => 65],
];
echo $party[1]["name"];
```
```output
Ben
```

## Adding, removing and searching

```php
<?php
$q = [2, 3];
array_push($q, 4);      // end
array_unshift($q, 1);   // start
$last = array_pop($q);  // removes 4
echo implode(",", $q), " | ", $last, "\n";
var_dump(in_array(3, $q), array_search(3, $q), array_key_exists(0, $q));
```
```output
1,2,3 | 4
bool(true)
int(2)
bool(true)
```

## Sorting

```php
<?php
$n = [5, 2, 9];
sort($n);   echo implode(",", $n), "\n";   // low to high
rsort($n);  echo implode(",", $n), "\n";   // high to low
$ages = ["Ana" => 30, "Ben" => 20];
asort($ages);  echo implode(",", array_keys($ages)), "\n";  // by value
ksort($ages);  echo implode(",", array_keys($ages));          // by key
```
```output
2,5,9
9,5,2
Ben,Ana
Ana,Ben
```

## Transforming arrays

```php
<?php
$nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
$doubled = array_map(fn($n) => $n * 2, $nums);
$evens = array_filter($nums, fn($n) => $n % 2 === 0);
$total = array_reduce($nums, fn($sum, $n) => $sum + $n, 0);
echo implode(",", $doubled), " | ", implode(",", $evens), " | ", $total;
```
```output
2,4,6,8,10 | 2,4 | 15
```

## Merging and destructuring

```php
<?php
$a = ["x" => 1];
$b = ["y" => 2];
print_r(array_merge($a, $b));
[$first, $second] = ["gold", "silver"];
echo $second;
```
```output
Array
(
    [x] => 1
    [y] => 2
)
silver
```

> TIP: `print_r()` is the easiest way to look inside an array while debugging.
remember: Indexes start at 0; `$arr[] = x` appends.
Use `foreach ($arr as $key => $value)` to loop through any array.
`array_map` transforms, `array_filter` keeps some, `array_reduce` combines.

title: CONTROL FLOW
intro: Control structures decide which code runs and how many times.
remember: `match` is strict (`===`) and returns a value.
`do...while` always runs once; `foreach` is the best loop for arrays.
`continue` skips one iteration; `break` leaves the loop.

title: FUNCTIONS
intro: A function is a named block of code you can reuse. It can take inputs (parameters) and give back a result with `return`.
remember: Use `return` to give a value back; `echo` only displays it.
Functions cannot see outside variables unless passed in (or captured with `use` / `fn`).
`&$param` lets a function change the caller's variable.

title: CLASSES & OBJECTS
intro: Object-oriented programming groups data (properties) and behaviour (methods) together. A class is the blueprint; an object is one thing built from it.
remember: `new` creates an object; `$this` is the current object.
Keep data `private` and expose it through methods.
Assigning an object does not copy it; use `clone` for a copy.

title: INHERITANCE, INTERFACES & TRAITS
intro: These tools let classes share and reuse code.
remember: `extends` = inherit from a class; `implements` = follow an interface; `use` = include a trait.
`parent::method()` calls the parent version of an overridden method.
`static` refers to the class that was actually called.

title: ERRORS & EXCEPTIONS
intro: Exceptions let you stop when something goes wrong and handle the problem in one place.
remember: `throw` raises an exception; `catch` handles it.
`finally` runs whether or not an exception happened.
Catch the most specific type you can.

title: FORMS, SESSIONS & SECURITY
intro: PHP was built for the web. It can read form data, remember users between pages and talk to the browser with cookies.
body:
## Superglobals

- `$_GET`: values from the URL, e.g. `page.php?id=5`.
- `$_POST`: values sent by a form with `method="post"`.
- `$_SESSION`: data kept on the server for one visitor.
- `$_COOKIE`: small values stored in the browser.
- `$_SERVER`: request info, e.g. `$_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"]`.

## Handling a form

```php
<form method="post" action="login.php">
    <input name="username">
    <input name="password" type="password">
    <button>Log in</button>
</form>
<?php
if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] === "POST") {
    $username = trim($_POST["username"] ?? "");
    if ($username === "") {
        echo "Username is required";
    }
}
```

> TIP: Use POST for passwords and anything that changes data. GET puts values in the URL, where they end up in history and logs.

## Validating input

```php
<?php
var_dump(filter_var("ana@example.com", FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL));
var_dump(filter_var("42abc", FILTER_VALIDATE_INT));
var_dump(filter_var("18", FILTER_VALIDATE_INT));
```
```output
string(15) "ana@example.com"
bool(false)
int(18)
```

## Escaping output (prevent XSS)

Never print user input straight into HTML. `htmlspecialchars()` turns special characters into safe entities.

```php
<?php
$comment = "<script>alert(1)</script>";
echo htmlspecialchars($comment, ENT_QUOTES, "UTF-8");
```
```output
<script>alert(1)</script>
```

## Sessions

```php
<?php
session_start();                 // call before any output
$_SESSION["user"] = "Ana";       // remember the user

// on another page:
session_start();
echo $_SESSION["user"] ?? "Guest";

// logging out:
session_unset();
session_destroy();
```

## Cookies

```php
<?php
setcookie("theme", "dark", time() + 86400 * 30, "/");  // 30 days
echo $_COOKIE["theme"] ?? "light";
```

## Storing passwords

```php
<?php
$hash = password_hash("secret123", PASSWORD_DEFAULT);
var_dump(password_verify("secret123", $hash));
var_dump(password_verify("wrong", $hash));
```
```output
bool(true)
bool(false)
```

> MISTAKE: Never store plain-text passwords, and never use `md5()` for them. Always use `password_hash()` and `password_verify()`.
remember: Validate input on the way in; escape it with `htmlspecialchars()` on the way out.
Call `session_start()` before using `$_SESSION`.
Hash passwords with `password_hash()`.

title: DATABASES WITH PDO
intro: PDO (PHP Data Objects) is the standard way to talk to databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQLite from PHP.
remember: Create a `PDO` object to connect; turn on exception mode.
`prepare()` + `execute([...])` for every query that uses outside data.
Pick a fetch method: `fetch`, `fetchAll` or `fetchColumn`.

title: MODERN PHP 8 FEATURES
intro: PHP 8 added many features that make code shorter and safer. Here are the ones you will see most.
remember: `?->` stops on null instead of crashing.
Enums give a fixed set of named values; `tryFrom()` returns null for unknown ones.
`readonly` properties can be set only once.
